evidence.quote: let renewalRefusal (today: DateOnly) (loan: Loan) (library: Library) : LendingError option =
NotRenewable = Loans.renewalRefusal today loan library |> Option.map renewalReason
| Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The renewal rule (overdue, then limit, then holds, in that order) lives in Tier 2 in renewalRefusal. Loans.renew and the new Loans.renewAll both use it, so loans, renew and renew-all cannot disagree. Tier 3 only calls Tier 2 and turns the LendingError into reason text (renewalReason); it adds no predicate of its own. The CLI only renders Tier 3 views, and the change removes the old CLI path that called Loans.renew directly.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect appears in Tier 1/2: renewalRefusal and renewAll are pure and take today and the library as arguments. Tier 3 reads the date through the Clock port and saves through the Store port via commit. The change also removes the CLI's direct Store.Load/Save and its direct call into Loans.renew (Tier 2), which fixes an existing ARC-BND-02 violation.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The renewal limit is defined once, as Policy.renewLimit, and both the Tier 2 guard and the Tier 3 view reference it; the refusal text takes the limit from the error value. The refusal order is defined once, in renewalRefusal. No literal or predicate is copied.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Two rules are new: the limit per member type, and which member's limit applies to a loan (the borrower's, with Standard as the fallback). Both are decided in Tier 2, in Policy.renewLimit and Loans.renewLimitOf. The Tier 3 view asks Tier 2 for the limit rather than working it out from the member record itself.

evidence.quote: |> Result.map (fun (l, loan) -> l, Views.ofRenew l loan))

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added anywhere. renewLimitOf is a pure lookup on the library value it is given, and use cases still load and save through the existing Store port via commit.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The per-type limits appear only in Policy.renewLimit, and the rule for which member's limit applies appears only in renewLimitOf. The refusal guard, the refusal reason and the renew view all use renewLimitOf, so the shown limit cannot drift from the enforced one. The old single constant is replaced, not left alongside the new rule.
